Name: IIS is up to date
Description: IIS should be running the latest available version with all security patches applied.
Rationale: Outdated IIS versions may contain known vulnerabilities that are exploitable remotely.
RemediationText: Ensure Windows Update is current and all IIS-related hotfixes are installed.

Name: Host Headers required on all sites
Description: IIS sites should require Host Headers to prevent host header injection attacks.
Rationale: Sites without host header requirements can be targeted via host header injection, leading to cache poisoning or SSRF.
RemediationText: Add a specific host header to each IIS site binding via IIS Manager or: Set-WebBinding -Name 'SiteName' -BindingInformation '*:80:' -PropertyName HostHeader -Value 'yourdomain.com'

Name: Request filtering enabled
Description: IIS Request Filtering module should be enabled to block malicious HTTP requests.
Rationale: Request filtering blocks known attack patterns such as path traversal, double-encoding, and oversized requests.
RemediationText: Install the Request Filtering module: Install-WindowsFeature Web-Request-Filtering

Name: HTTP TRACE method disabled
Description: The HTTP TRACE method should be disabled to prevent cross-site tracing (XST) attacks.
Rationale: TRACE echoes request headers back to the client, which can expose cookies and session tokens via XSS.
RemediationText: Add TRACE to the denied verbs list in Request Filtering, or use: Add-WebConfigurationProperty -Filter 'system.webServer/security/requestFiltering/verbs' -PSPath 'IIS:\' -Name '.' -Value @{verb='TRACE';allowed='false'}

Name: Maximum URL length restricted
Description: IIS should reject requests with URLs exceeding a reasonable length to prevent buffer overflow and DoS attacks.
Rationale: Unrestricted URL lengths enable attacks that exploit vulnerable URL parsing code.

Name: Anonymous authentication disabled on sensitive paths
Description: Anonymous authentication should be disabled on administrative or sensitive application paths.
Rationale: Anonymous authentication allows unauthenticated access to resources that may be sensitive.
RemediationText: Disable anonymous authentication on sites/applications that do not require it.

Name: Windows Authentication using Kernel-mode enabled
Description: Kernel-mode authentication improves performance and security for Windows Authentication.
Rationale: Kernel-mode auth is more resistant to certain Kerberos delegation attacks than user-mode auth.
RemediationText: Enable kernel-mode authentication in IIS Manager > Authentication > Windows Authentication > Advanced Settings.

Name: SSL 3.0 disabled
Description: SSL 3.0 is a deprecated protocol vulnerable to POODLE attack and should be disabled.
Rationale: SSL 3.0 allows downgrade attacks and has known cryptographic weaknesses (POODLE).
RemediationText: Disable SSL 3.0 via registry: Set HKLM\...\SSL 3.0\Server\Enabled = 0

Name: TLS 1.0 disabled
Description: TLS 1.0 is deprecated and vulnerable to BEAST and POODLE-for-TLS attacks.
Rationale: TLS 1.0 no longer meets PCI DSS requirements and has known weaknesses.
RemediationText: Disable TLS 1.0 via registry: Set HKLM\...\TLS 1.0\Server\Enabled = 0

Name: TLS 1.1 disabled
Description: TLS 1.1 is deprecated and should be disabled in favour of TLS 1.2 or 1.3.
Rationale: TLS 1.1 lacks many modern security features and is considered weak by current standards.
RemediationText: Disable TLS 1.1 via registry: Set HKLM\...\TLS 1.1\Server\Enabled = 0

Name: TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 enabled
Description: TLS 1.2 (minimum) or TLS 1.3 must be enabled to provide secure transport.
Rationale: Disabling all modern TLS versions would break HTTPS. Verify TLS 1.2 is ON before disabling older versions.
RemediationText: Enable TLS 1.2: Set HKLM\...\TLS 1.2\Server\Enabled = 1 and DisabledByDefault = 0

Name: IIS version hidden from HTTP response headers
Description: The Server HTTP response header should not reveal the IIS version number.
Rationale: Version disclosure helps attackers target known vulnerabilities for the specific IIS version.

Name: Directory browsing disabled
Description: IIS directory browsing should be disabled to prevent listing of server files.
Rationale: Directory listings expose application structure and file names that can aid attackers in reconnaissance.

Name: ASP.NET error details not exposed to remote users
Description: ASP.NET detailed error messages should only be shown locally, not to remote clients.
Rationale: Detailed error messages reveal stack traces, file paths, connection strings and other sensitive internals.
RemediationText: Set customErrors mode='RemoteOnly' in web.config or IIS configuration.

Name: IIS logging enabled
Description: IIS logging must be enabled on all sites to support incident investigation.
Rationale: Without access logs there is no audit trail for attacks, data access or compliance purposes.
RemediationText: Enable logging in IIS Manager > site > Logging, or: Set-WebConfigurationProperty -Filter 'system.applicationHost/sites/siteDefaults/logFile' -PSPath 'IIS:\' -Name 'enabled' -Value $true

Name: IIS log files stored outside the web root
Description: Log files should not be stored inside the web root where they could be downloaded by visitors.
Rationale: Log files may contain IP addresses, session tokens and URI parameters that expose user behaviour.
RemediationText: Move IIS log directory to a path outside the web root (e.g. C:\IISLogs).
